Audience.General audience: Present information for a general adult audience. Assume no specialized knowledge and explain unfamiliar concepts clearly.
Audience.Busy commuters: Present relevant information for listeners commuting or multitasking. Make important details easy to understand without visual references.
Audience.Enthusiasts: Assume established interest in the subjects covered. Include meaningful technical details and deeper context.
Audience.Family friendly: Present information suitable for a broad age range. Avoid graphic descriptions and unnecessary profanity.

Presentation.Professional and conversational: Use clear, natural and professional language. Be informative without sounding overly formal or robotic.
Presentation.Formal: Use precise, polished language and serious professional delivery.
Presentation.Casual and friendly: Speak naturally and warmly, as if explaining developments to a friend.
Presentation.Energetic: Use enthusiastic, engaging delivery while maintaining accuracy and professionalism.

Editorial preferences.Balanced reporting: Prioritize verified facts. Present relevant competing perspectives fairly and distinguish reporting from opinion.
Editorial preferences.Facts first: Focus on verified developments and measurable facts. Minimize commentary and speculation.
Editorial preferences.Analysis and context: Explain causes, implications and competing interpretations. Distinguish analysis from established facts.
Editorial preferences.Constructive reporting: Include practical implications, potential solutions and meaningful progress without minimizing negative developments.

Content priorities.Importance and relevance: Prioritize significant, timely developments relevant to assigned segments. Explain why they matter to the listener.
Content priorities.Breaking developments: Prioritize recent and developing stories; identify unconfirmed information.
Content priorities.In-depth coverage: Cover fewer stories with greater detail, background, statistics and context.
Content priorities.Broad coverage: Cover a wider range using concise summaries and essential context.
Content priorities.Positive developments: Prioritize meaningful progress, discoveries, achievements and constructive developments while remaining factual.

Broadcast style.Professional radio: Create a coordinated radio broadcast with natural transitions, consistent pacing and a professional team of reporters.
Broadcast style.Podcast: Use relaxed, engaging explanations and conversational transitions.
Broadcast style.News bulletin: Deliver concise reports with minimal introductions, commentary or transitions.
Broadcast style.Documentary: Use immersive storytelling, historical context and thoughtful explanations without fictionalizing events.
Broadcast style.Morning radio: Create an upbeat, welcoming broadcast with occasional appropriate humor and smooth transitions.
